How a Jupiter QPSK modem image is built

From the Simulink model to a BOOT.BIN on the board: the model overlay stack, what is changed in the generated HDL afterwards, the two Vivado sessions, and every other tool in the chain.

Describes the sp3 single-image chain that produced the deployed sp3txclk pair (2026-09-13). Paths are relative to the repository root unless they start with /.

0Overview

One script, modem/build_image.sh, drives three stages. The first stage runs on the build workstation (MATLAB R2025b and a local Vivado 2025.1 for block-design work), the second is Verilator simulation, and the third is synthesis on the remote host hdl-dev-2. Every stage ends by printing a token that the next stage greps for. The diagram reads left to right; the line under each box is the token that proves the stage finished.

1Entry point and stages

The recommended launch keeps the whole run in a transient user unit so it survives the shell that started it:

systemd-run --user --collect --same-dir --unit sp3-build-$(date +%s) \
  bash -c 'modem/build_image.sh --tag sp3 --remote-base /mnt/disk2/scratch/qpsk-builds \
           > /mnt/onetb/scratch/qpsk-build-trees/work_sp3/build.out 2>&1'
Option or defaultMeaning
--tag sp3Kit name becomes jupiter_byte_sp3_build; the tag is carried into every stamp and the image name.
--workDefault /mnt/onetb/scratch/qpsk-build-trees/work_sp3. Holds STAMP.hdl, STAMP.gates, STAMP.vivado, the fetched log and the finished image.
--regen-parentDefault /mnt/onetb/scratch/qpsk-build-trees/regen11. The fresh kit is created under it.
--remote-baseWhere the kit lands on hdl-dev-2. Use the second disk; the home filesystem there is nearly full.
--from, --stop-afterSelect a stage range. A later stage refuses to run unless the previous stamp carries the same model_tree_sha.
--dryRuns the script with a PATH shim that turns every rsync into rsync -n, because the kit's own build script deletes on the remote before its dry gate.
WNS_FLOOR=0.005Gate 2 floor in nanoseconds on the modem clock axi_adrv9001_adc_1_clk.

Each stage writes <work>/STAMP.<stage> with the fields stage= tag= model_tree_sha= git= when= result=. The model_tree_sha is a sha256 over the sorted list of generated Verilog files in the kit, so a regenerated model invalidates every later stamp automatically.

2Simulink model build flow

The two models

modem/dev/commhdlQPSKTxRx.slx is the source model, derived from the MathWorks commhdlQPSKTxRx example by way of the Analog Devices TransceiverToolbox. It is edited in place by the overlay scripts. modem/dev/commhdlQPSKTxRxLoopback.slx is the design under test. It is cloned from the source model on every assemble, and its HDL subsystem is commhdlQPSKTxRxLoopback/TxRxComposite. Both .slx files are mutable as-built artefacts, which is why they show as modified after a build.

Driver chain

  1. modem/build_hdl.sh <regen-parent> --kit-name jupiter_byte_<tag>_build --complete-bd copies modem/ into a fresh kit with rsync (excluding hdl_prj_*, slprj, s1_rtl*) and rewrites the kit path in every .m file with sed.
  2. It exports the environment that is the image configuration (next table) and runs timeout 5400 matlab -batch build_variant_byte.
  3. modem/dev/build_variant_byte.m runs the TransceiverToolbox setup.m, puts the kit last on the MATLAB path so its parameters win, calls hdlsetuptoolpath for the local Vivado, deletes hdl_prj_jupiter_composite and slprj to defeat smart-build caching, then runs assemble_jupiter_240k5_byte.m followed by hdlworkflow_loopback.m.

The environment is the image configuration. build_hdl.sh exports:

QPSK_LEAN=1  QPSK_FRAME=f1536  QPSK_SPS=4  QPSK_BEATFIX=1  QPSK_BEATOBS=1
QPSK_FRAMESTAT=1  QPSK_RXFIX=1  QPSK_TXFIX="${QPSK_TXFIX-1}"

modem/common/model/frame_config_k5.m is the single source of truth for frame geometry and defaults to the older k5 frame at 8 samples per symbol. Running the MATLAB entry point without these exports silently builds a different rung. QPSK_RXFIX cannot be turned off by the caller; QPSK_TXFIX= (empty) is the documented way to build the no-TX-fix discriminating image.

Overlay stack inside assemble

modem/dev/assemble_jupiter_240k5_byte.m is 650 lines of ordered edits to the model, followed by hard gates. The file name is historical; the deployed configuration is the f1536 frame at 4 samples per symbol.

PhaseScriptsWhat changes
0patch_hdlworkflow_counters.m, _taps.m, _forensic.m, _loopgain.m, simulink/beatila/patch_hdlworkflow_beatfix.m, rxfix/patch_hdlworkflow_rxfix.mIdempotent text patches to hdlworkflow_loopback.m that add AXI4-Lite register mappings for each instrument or fix.
0brate_240k_overlay.m, ss8_fix_overlay.m, timing_hardening_overlay.m, agc_gain_range_overlay.mEdits to the source model: sample times expressed as 1/(Rsym*SamplesPerSymbol), symbol-sync fixes, pipeline registers, AGC range.
1build_composite_local.mClones the source model to the loopback model, creates TxRxComposite, duplicates Transmitter and Receiver, adds the RX source mux and rate transitions, deletes simulation-only blocks, sets the HDL subsystem.
1.5 to 2.12msggen_rom_overlay_k5.m, variant_pre.m, fec_insert_overlay_rxonly_k5.m, FEC counter/skip/capture overlays, taps_240k5_overlay.m, rx_framing_overlay_k5.m, adc_forensic_overlay.m, iq_debug_tap_overlay.m, canary and loop-tune overlaysMessage ROM, receive-side FEC, debug taps, framing, ADC forensic capture, canary registers.
2.13 to 2.16byte_tx_overlay_k5.m, fec_tx_encoder_overlay_k5.m, byte_rx_overlay_k5.m, byte_plumbing_overlay_k5.m, byte_rxfifo_overlay.mThe byte plane: 64-bit byte DMA ports both ways, TX encoder, and the retarget to the reference design JUPITER (RX & TX, BYTE DMA) through AnalogDevices.jupiter.plugin_rd_rxtx_byte.
2.17 to 2.21resolver_lookback_fix.m, loop_gain_axi_overlay.m, framestat_overlay.m, beatobs/beatfix overlays, rxfix/rxfix_w1_overlay.m, rxfix_steer_overlay.m, rxfix_r1_overlay.m, rxfix_bs_overlay.m, rxfix_pad_overlay.m, rxfix/txfix_f3_overlay.mEnvironment-gated fixes. In the sp3 chain these model overlays replace the netlist injections of the sp2 chain (section 3).

After the overlays the script writes a description string into the model (frame=… variant=… build=…), saves it, and runs the pre-synthesis gates. The gates assert that the kit parameters are active (samples per symbol matches the frame config), that the symbol rate times samples per symbol equals the 15.36 MHz model rail, and that the CFO change-detect threshold is the expected value.

HDL Workflow Advisor configuration

modem/dev/hdlworkflow_loopback.m is the exported Workflow Advisor script (R2025b). The fixed settings that matter:

SettingValue
Reference designJUPITER (RX & TX, BYTE DMA), project jupiter_sdr, design rxtx, four 16-bit inputs, one valid
DeviceZynq UltraScale+ xczu3eg-sfva625-2-e, platform AnalogDevices JUPITER
Language, workflowVerilog, IP Core Generation, project folder hdl_prj_jupiter_composite
Synthesis toolXilinx Vivado 2025.1, unsupported-version override on, IP caching off
Custom build scriptCI/scripts/adi_build.tcl from the TransceiverToolbox; build_env_jupiter.sh at the repository root sets its ADI_* job and cache variables
Run orderStage 1 generates RTL and packages the IP core; Stage 2 creates the project and software interface and builds. Program-device is off.

Port to interface map

Model portReference design interface
adc_dataInI, adc_dataInQ, adc_validInADRV9002 ADC Data I0/Q0, IP Valid Rx Data IN
tx_dataOutI, tx_dataOutQ, tx_validOutADRV9002 DAC Data I0/Q0, IP Load Tx Data OUT
host_txI, host_txQ, host_txValidIP Data 0/1 IN, IP Valid Tx Data IN
debugI1/Q1, debugI/Q, debugValidIP Data 0/1 OUT, IP Data 2/3 OUT, IP Data Valid OUT (the RX capture DMA)
byte_data, byte_valid, byte_first, byte_readyByte Data IN [0:63], Byte Valid IN, Byte First IN, Byte Ready OUT
byte_rx_data, byte_rx_valid, byte_rx_last, byte_rx_user, byte_rx_readyByte Data OUT [0:63], Byte Valid/Last/User OUT, Byte Ready IN
AXI4-Lite registersModem base 0x9D000000. Counters at 0x100 to 0x108, source selects 0x114/0x118, TX data source 0x158, fix control fixctl at 0x208, RXFIX witness words 0x214 to 0x25C. The host-side truth for 0x208 and up is modem/regmap/regmap.toml.

The platform DMAs come from the plugin, not the model: rx_byte_dma at 0x9D200000, tx_byte_dma at 0x9D100000, byte_ctrl_gpio at 0x9D300000.

What HDL Coder leaves behind

  • hdl_prj_jupiter_composite/hdlsrc/commhdlQPSKTxRxLoopback/: generated Verilog, every module prefixed TxRxCompo_ip_src_, plus the generated model and the resource report.
  • hdl_prj_jupiter_composite/ipcore/TxRxCompo_ip_v1_0.zip: the packaged IP core. Every later netlist edit must patch the loose Verilog, the unpacked ipcore copy and the zip members together.
  • hdl_prj_jupiter_composite/vivado_ip_prj/vivado_prj.xpr and system.bd: the ADI reference project, which must already contain the byte_breakout cell.

The Create Project task fails by design. The ADI add_ip step passes the ipcore directory where Vivado wants the zip path, so the MATLAB batch exits non-zero. build_hdl.sh ignores the exit code and gates on the three artefacts above instead. The block design is then completed by the repository's own Tcl (section 3).

The TransceiverToolbox checkout at /home/tcollins/dev/qpsk_ai/TransceiverToolbox (commit 11f5cf94) carries the Analog Devices HDL tree vendored inside it. It is a read-only donor: nothing in this repository edits it, and it is not a git submodule.

3Changes made after HDL Coder

Steps 4 to 7 of build_hdl.sh take the generated tree and turn it into a kit that can be synthesised without MATLAB. Everything here is scripted and leaves a token in the log.

StepTool and fileWhat changesProof
4amodem/common/rxfifo/rxfifo_inject.sh <kit> 4096Replaces HDL Coder's 64-deep register ByteRxFifo with the hand-written block-RAM module modem/common/rxfifo/ByteRxFifo.v in every loose, ipcore and zip copy. This is a tracked design source, not an instrument.RXFIFO_INJECT_OK files+zips=N
4instruments/txcap/txcap_inject.py, then TXMARK=1 instruments/ddrcap/ddrcap_inject.py, then instruments/ddrcap2/ddrcap2_inject.pyPython netlist injectors that add the TX frame-start port and the DDR capture instrument taps. Each patches the Verilog, both zip members and component.xml. Order matters: txcap creates the port that ddrcap anchors on.Each returns 0; a failure is fatal.
5One local Vivado session, complete_bd_run.tcl, sourcing complete_byte_bd.tcl, instruments/ddrcap/ddrcap_bd.tcl, seqbist_bd.tclAdds the ipcore zip to the catalog, instantiates TxRxCompo_ip_0 at 0x9D000000 on axi_adrv9001/adc_1_clk, wires ADC/DAC data and valids through the sync cells, asserts the byte breakout and byte DMAs exist, sets the RX byte DMA cyclic, wires the byte DMA interrupts (wire_byte_irqs.tcl prints BYTE_IRQ_MAP with the two interrupt cells the device tree needs), adds constraints, validates. Then repoints the rx2 DMA at the DDR capture ports and adds the sequence-BIST traffic generator, checker and three GPIO blocks at 0x9D400000 to 0x9D450000 (skip with SP3_SKIP_SEQBIST=1).BYTE_WIRE_OK VALIDATE_OK COMPLETE_BYTE_BD_DONE DDRCAP_BD_WIRE_OK SEQBIST_WIRE_OK COMPLETE_BD_RUN_DONE, then BUILD_HDL_BD_OK. The script also fails if the .xpr contains an absolute file path, which would break on the remote host.
6modem/vivado/txfix_build.sh.tmpl, txfix_build.tcl.tmpl, modem/instruments/txclk/pre_synth.tcl, txclk_bd.tclKit assembly. The templates become build_txfix.sh and build_txfix.tcl in the kit. The txclk pair is the deployed clock fix: at synthesis time it sets USE_RX_CLK_FOR_TX1=1 on axi_adrv9001 so the DAC path runs on the modem's ADC clock and the modem-to-DAC crossing becomes a same-clock path (skip with SP3_SKIP_TXCLK=1). Stale txcdc files from the superseded FIFO attempt are removed. TXFIX_VARIANT and SEQBIST_VARIANT stamps are written.BUILD_HDL_KIT_OK
7grep checks in build_hdl.shConfirms the overlay-produced modules exist in the generated tree (RxW1Census, RxSteer, PdPopIndex, BsSeamCensus, FixCtlDec, padCount, fullRAM) and that the byte serialiser's ready path was padded by exactly four registers. Optional --diff-bank diffs the RTL against the banked tree.MODEL_OVERLAYS_OK BS_READY_PAD_OK

The sp2 chain, kept for rollback rebuilds. Before sp3, the fixes now applied as model overlays were injected into a banked, already-generated netlist. modem/fixes/apply_fixes.py --manifest --role A|B reads modem/fixes/fixes.toml, verifies the banked base tree jupiter_byte_ddrcap2_build by sha256, then runs the TX fix injector (F3), the sequence-BIST kit patcher and the RX fix injector (rxfix_inject.py, variants W1, R4B, R4D, R1, BS, PAD) in order. Role A is board 148 with W1 R4B BS PAD; role B is board 146 with W1 R4D R1. That chain still rebuilds the shipped rollback pair and must not be edited casually: some strings it emits are byte-for-byte in deployed silicon.

4Simulation gate (stage gates, Gate 1)

The generated tree is proven equivalent to the banked reference before any synthesis time is spent.

  1. modem/rtl_sim/make_sro_trees.sh --from-regen <kit> builds a simulation tree, stripping the TxRxCompo_ip_src_ prefixes and emitting model wrappers.
  2. modem/rtl_sim/tree_marker.sh <tree> <name> for W1, R4B, R4DR1, BS, PAD and F3 must each report the fix came from the model, not from an injector.
  3. modem/gates/run_gates.sh --legs modem/gates/model_matrix.legs runs each leg of the table as its own systemd-run --user unit under Verilator 5.020, scores with score_matrix.py against reference_loss.toml, and reuses content-keyed .ok files. It first runs base_tree.sh verify-bank against modem/gates/bank.sha256.

The stage passes only on GATES_DONE … fail=0. It refuses to start while any sp2-gate-* unit is running, because the tree and object directories are shared. Skipping the stage with --from vivado prints an explicit warning that the build is ungated.

5Remote synthesis, implementation and bootgen (stage vivado, Gate 2)

Launch from the workstation

build_image.sh runs the kit's build_txfix.sh with IMPL_STRATEGY=explore. That script:

  • checks the kit name matches the accepted patterns and that TXFIX_VARIANT exists;
  • checks the remote build base has at least 25 GB free and that no other txfix-build-* or ddrcap-build-* unit is active (override with ALLOW_CONCURRENT=1);
  • copies the kit with rsync -a --delete, excluding old runs, caches and any previous BOOT.BIN;
  • launches the build through ssh as a transient unit and returns immediately:
ssh hdl-dev-2 ... bash -s <<'REMOTE'
export PATH=/opt/Xilinx/2025.1/Vivado/bin:/usr/bin:/bin
systemd-run --user --unit="$UNIT" --collect --working-directory="$Z" \
  bash -c "timeout 14400 vivado -mode batch -notrace -source $REMOTE_DIR/build_txfix.tcl \
           > $REMOTE_DIR/build_txfix_vivado.log 2>&1"
REMOTE

build_image.sh then polls systemctl --user is-active on the remote once a minute (four-hour cap), fetches the log, the routed timing reports and vivado_ip_prj/boot/BOOT.BIN with rsync, and requires TXFIX_BUILD_DONE in the log.

What runs on hdl-dev-2

build_txfix.tcl, with the current directory set to the Vivado project:

  1. Opens the project, rebuilds the IP catalog, then sources pre_synth.tcl if the kit has one (PRE_SYNTH_HOOK_OK). This is where the txclk block-design change is applied.
  2. Generates the block design, runs synthesis with the requested job count.
  3. Sources timing_gate.tcl: opens the synthesised design and reports worst negative slack on paths into the modem IP only (TIMING_GATE_WNS). It fails only below a loose floor, default minus 1 ns, so it catches broken designs rather than tight ones.
  4. Runs implementation. With IMPL_STRATEGY=explore the place directive is ExtraTimingOpt and physical optimisation, routing and post-route physical optimisation use AggressiveExplore.
  5. Reads the routed worst negative slack; if it is negative the script prints TXFIX_ROUTED_TIMING_FAIL and stops before bootgen.
  6. Copies impl_1/system_top.bit and the boot components from the vendored ADI tree, then packages the boot image:
set b projects/common/boot/jupiter_sdr
foreach f {u-boot.elf zynq.bif fsbl.elf bl31.elf pmufw.elf regs.init} { file copy $b/$f boot/$f }
cd boot; exec bootgen -arch zynqmp -image zynq.bif -o BOOT.BIN -w

There is no XSA or hardware hand-off export. The first-stage boot loader, PMU firmware, ARM trusted firmware and U-Boot are the pre-built binaries shipped in the reference design.

Gate 2: the modem clock

Back on the workstation, python3 modem/gates/modem_wns.py <impl_1 reports> --clock axi_adrv9001_adc_1_clk --min 0.005 reads the intra-clock table of the post-route physical-optimisation timing summary and prints MODEM_CLK_WNS clock= wns= tns= failing= total=. Below the floor the build stops with BUILD_IMAGE_GATE2_FAIL; the rule is to record it and not to retry with other strategies. On pass the image is copied to <work>/BOOT.BIN.jupiter.<tag>.<md5> and BUILD_IMAGE_DONE is printed.

ImageModem-clock WNS (ns)
rxfixpad (sp2 base)0.105
sp2A / sp2B0.447 / 0.785
sp30.785
sp3txclk (deployed)1.392

Two other slack numbers appear in the log and are not Gate 2: the pre-implementation figure in the TXFIX_BUILD_DONE wns= line, and the whole-design routed figure. Only the intra-clock post-route row for the modem clock is the gate.

6Image bank, kernel, device tree and deploy (Gate 3)

Bank

Finished images are copied by hand into images/ as BOOT.BIN.jupiter.<tag>.<md5> (one file per image, no aliases; the flash rails resolve FLASH_MD5 through images/MD5SUMS). images/MD5SUMS is authoritative, images/README.md holds one provenance row per image, and images/CURRENT.txt maps role A (board 148) and role B (board 146) to the image each should boot. The deployed pair is sp3prod b68dbf1d9321 on both roles (2026-09-16); sp3txclk cae8c4fdac09 is banked as the rollback.

Kernel and device tree

  • Kernel: images/Image.6.12.77-uio.<sha>.gz, built once from the Analog Devices xlnx/release/v6.12.y-2026r1 branch with modem/boot/kernel-arm64-cmdline-extend.patch, generic UIO built in and the UIO match id on the kernel command line. It is cross-compiled with the Xilinx 2025.1 aarch64-linux-gnu- toolchain; the recipe lives in the Sphinx page on building and flashing, not in a script.
  • Device tree: modem/boot/qpsk_byte_uio.dtso adds three generic-UIO nodes for the byte DMAs and control GPIO and a 2 MB carve. ops/deploy_dtb.sh build <tx> <rx> substitutes the two interrupt cells reported by BYTE_IRQ_MAP, compiles with dtc -@, merges into the pristine base tree with fdtoverlay, and check round-trips the result through dtc and asserts the nodes with fdtget.

Deploy order for a fresh board

  1. ops/deploy_kernel.sh <ip>
  2. ops/deploy_dtb.sh <ip>
  3. ops/deploy_image.sh <ip> A|B (reads images/CURRENT.txt)
  4. ops/provision.sh <ip>: copies the host application sources and profiles, builds the host app natively on the board with plain gcc (not make), installs the lock watchdog.

All four use ops/anyssh.sh and ops/askpass.sh (password auth through SSH_ASKPASS), stage files under /root, check size and magic bytes, back up /boot, reboot and wait on ping. Plain scp to these boards writes zero-byte files, which is why the helper exists.

Flash rails

On the live rig, images go on through ops/flash/flash_148_txfix.sh and ops/flash/flash_146_txfix.sh, launched with ops/launch_rig_unit.sh so each runs as a transient unit from a frozen copy of the script. A rail checks preconditions and the on-board backup, flashes, reads back the md5, runs the arm gate (148 only) or the both-board bring-up (146), and on any failure rolls back to the .bak image and ends. Gate 3 is then the credited packet-error-rate windows scored by ops/accept_analyze.py with lost frames in the denominator.

Host software

host/Makefile builds qpsk_tun, qpsk_capture, qpsk_perf and the modem_status ncurses status tool with gcc. Unit tests run on the x86 workstation with make -C host test. On the boards the tools are compiled natively (148 is arm64, 146 is armhf) inside the on-board host app directory that provision.sh creates. The register header host/qpsk_fixregs.h is generated from modem/regmap/regmap.toml by modem/regmap/gen_regmap.py; --check is a CI gate.

9Known traps

  • Running the MATLAB entry point without the QPSK_* exports builds the k5 rung at 8 samples per symbol. Always go through build_hdl.sh.
  • The MATLAB batch exits non-zero at Create Project on every successful build. The artefact gate is the real check.
  • build_txfix.sh --dry is positional. Setting DRY=1 in the environment launches a real two-hour build. Other rig scripts have the opposite default, so read each script's header.
  • The wns= value in TXFIX_BUILD_DONE is the pre-implementation number. Gate 2 is only the MODEM_CLK_WNS line.
  • The .slx files show as modified after any assemble. That is expected; they are as-built artefacts.
  • A netlist edit that touches only the loose Verilog and not both zip members produces a kit whose synthesised design silently lacks the change. Every injector verifies the zip with unzip -p | strings | grep.
  • arm148_mode1.sh is for board 148 only; the same arm hangs board 146.
  • Never edit a script that a live unit is running. launch_rig_unit.sh runs a frozen copy for this reason.
  • The home filesystem on hdl-dev-2 is nearly full. Build under /mnt/disk2/scratch/qpsk-builds.
